title: Must this counter be approximate?
description: You estimate 50 million distinct tags in a day. At roughly 64 bytes per tag, one exact count map is about 3.2 GB before adding window buckets. A small shard fleet can hold the measured bucket state with headroom. Product permits approximate counts but does not require them. Which baseline is best justified?

options.text: Use a count-min sketch immediately because any billion-event stream is too large for exact counting.
options.explanation: Event volume is not the same as distinct-key state. The measured cardinality and bucket footprint make exact counting affordable here.

options.text: Keep exact key-sharded counters and budget the window buckets explicitly; introduce sketches if cardinality or list variants make memory expensive.
options.explanation: Choose approximation from state size and required precision, not just stream size. Exact counting is a clear baseline when it fits, while sketches remain an option for growth.

options.text: Retain only the current global top 100 and discard all other tag counts.
options.explanation: An item outside today's top 100 may become a leader later. Discarding all other counts loses the information needed to recognize that change.

options.text: Store each incoming event in the API process and sort the full history on every read.
options.explanation: That couples 50,000 reads/s to raw-event processing and grows state with event count rather than the bounded counter representation.
